references.text: Earlier in the chapter, the tunic, turban, and sash are mentioned as part of the holy garments for Aaron and his sons.
Describes the execution of the command to make the tunic from fine linen, along with the turban and sash featuring embroidered work.
Uses the same Hebrew expression for embroidered work (מַעֲשֵׂה רֹקֵם) as in the description of the veil.
Also mentions embroidered work (רֹקֵם) in connection with the entrance to the courtyard.
Moses dresses Aaron in the tunic as part of the consecration ceremony.
Aaron's sons are also clothed in tunics and turbans as prescribed.
The high priest is to wear the holy linen tunic and linen turban on the Day of Atonement.
The high priest Joshua receives a clean turban on his head as a sign of cleansing and restoration.
Both illustrate the principle of 'skillful weaving' and the combination of noble materials in the priest's service.
Fulfillment reference: Describes how the sash's specific requirements for embroidered work and linen were carried out in practice.
Fulfillment reference: Confirms that the turban made of fine linen was crafted as commanded in the source verse.
